How many words is the seed phrase you\'re importing?
A seed phrase is a list of 12 or 24 ordinary words that works as the master key to your account. Your wallet, your chatting address and your messages all come from it.
Anyone who has these words can take everything in your account. If you lose them and lose this device, nobody can get your account back, not even KaChat.
Write the words on paper, in order, and keep them somewhere safe and private. Never type them into a website, send them in a chat, or keep them in a screenshot or cloud notes.
12 words are already very secure. 24 words add even more protection.

Keeps your chat history in %1$s in the folder above (choosing All Files resets to the default %2$s folder). Automatic Sync keeps your devices in near-live sync: new messages upload moments after they arrive, and while the app is open it also watches the server and quietly pulls in what your other devices upload, fastest while you are in a chat. A wallet that connects to an existing backup restores it once automatically. Every upload merges with what is already on the server, so no device can erase another\'s history. Restoring merges the archive into this device\'s history.

A .kas domain can\'t be sent to a quantum-safe or other script address: KNS could never move it out again. Send it to a regular address instead.
